key_decisions.rationale: Preserves conditional guilt, capital threshold, acceptance of death, denial, protection from political surrender, and appeal.
key_decisions.before: If I am guilty of wrongdoing and have done something deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing to these charges against me, no one can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar.”
key_decisions.after: If I am guilty of wrongdoing and have done anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing to their charges against me, no one can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: If then I am doing wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die; but if there is nothing to their charges, no one is able to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar.”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves Festus's distancing vocabulary, disputed issues, Jesus' reported death, Paul, and life claim.
key_decisions.before: Instead, they had certain disputes with him about their own religion and about a man named Jesus who had died but whom Paul claimed was alive.
key_decisions.after: Instead, they had certain disputes with him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus whom Paul claimed was alive.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: but they had certain disputes with him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
